- Search for the bare form of a word: a search matches inside longer words, so "timeout" also finds "timeouts", and a Hebrew word without its prefix letters (חוזה, not בחוזה) finds every form of it.
- read_document reads a line range. Read around search hits before you rely on them.
- get_document_overview returns the outline, log profile, and the start and end of a file.
- analyze_whole_document reads the entire file in parts. Use it only when the task needs all of the file and cannot be done by matching text: a full summary, a timeline, or items that must be judged by meaning. It is slow and costly, and it can miss items of a long list.

functionDeclarations.name: search_document
functionDeclarations.description: Search a large attached file. mode "keywords" returns the most relevant passages for a question; "exact" finds the lines that contain the text; "regex" finds the lines that match a JavaScript regular expression (\w and \b know the letters of every language). For exact and regex, total_matching_lines counts every matching line, and the result shows the first max_results of them and the last one; search again from next_from_line for the ones after those shown, or with order "last" for the last ones. To count by group (per hour or day, per error code, per message shape), pass group_by: the result then counts each group, and shows no lines. from_line and to_line search part of the file. Results include line numbers to read further with read_document.

document_id.description: The document_id from the file's card.

query.description: Keywords, exact text, or a regex, depending on mode.

max_results.description: Up to 50 for exact/regex (default 20), up to 200 groups with group_by (default 50), up to 10 passages for keywords (default 5).

context_lines.description: exact/regex only: lines to show before and after each match, 0-5.

from_line.description: Search only from this line on (1-based). Pass a result's next_from_line to see the matches after those it shows.

to_line.description: Search only up to this line.

order.description: exact/regex only: "last" shows the last max_results matching lines (in file order) instead of the first. Defaults to "first".

group_by.description: exact/regex only: count the matching lines by group instead of showing them. "capture": by the text of the regex's first (group); "minute", "hour", "day": by the timestamp on the line; "shape": by the line with its numbers, IDs and quoted values taken out.

whole_word.description: exact only: match the text only as a whole word, not inside a longer one. Defaults to false.

functionDeclarations.name: read_document
functionDeclarations.description: Read a range of lines from a large attached file, with line numbers. Up to 600 lines per call; long results are cut and tell you where to continue.

document_id.description: The document_id from the file's card.

end_line.description: Last line to read. Defaults to start_line + 199.

functionDeclarations.name: get_document_overview
functionDeclarations.description: Get the full outline (headings with line numbers), log profile (levels, time range, most frequent errors), and the first and last lines of a large attached file.

document_id.description: The document_id from the file's card.

functionDeclarations.name: analyze_whole_document
functionDeclarations.description: Read an entire large file in parts and answer a task that needs all of it, such as a full summary, a timeline, or items that must be judged by meaning. To count or list lines that contain a word, an ID or a pattern, use search_document in exact or regex mode instead: its count is exact, and this can miss items. Slow and costly: prefer search_document and read_document for specific questions.

document_id.description: The document_id from the file's card.

task.description: What to find or produce from the whole file, stated completely.

output.description: "answer" (the default): one answer written from the notes of every part, for a summary, a timeline, or a description of events. "items": to count the items of a kind that must be judged by meaning, such as the clauses that set a fine: each part lists them, each with its line and a quote checked against the file, and the result counts them, by label.
